name: Secure Computation (MPC, FHE, ZK)
description: Secure multiparty computation, homomorphic encryption, zero-knowledge proofs, and private set operations.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this area focused on a narrow but practical question: how do you run machine learning on data you are not allowed to see? XONN: XNOR-based Oblivious Deep Neural Network Inference (2019) pushed oblivious neural-network inference toward real efficiency by reducing networks to XNOR operations, and Visor: Privacy-Preserving Video Analytics as a Cloud Service (2020) extended the same privacy-as-a-service idea to video. Alongside this, a second thread tackled encrypted data systems and search, with SEAL: Attack Mitigation for Encrypted Databases via Adjustable Leakage (2020) and DatashareNetwork: A Decentralized Privacy-Preserving Search Engine for Investigative Journalists (2020) showing that even encrypted databases and search engines leak, and that leakage must be measured and managed.

The early 2020s brought foundational cryptographic building blocks and the rise of private set operations. Poseidon: A New Hash Function for Zero-Knowledge Proof Systems (2021), now by far the most cited paper in the list, gave SNARK/STARK systems a hash function actually designed for proof circuits, becoming a workhorse primitive across the ZK ecosystem. At the same time private set intersection matured beyond a textbook problem into deployable tools, from Fuzzy Labeled Private Set Intersection with Applications to Private Real-Time Biometric Search (2021) to a real surveillance-scale deployment in Estimating Incidental Collection in Foreign Intelligence Surveillance (2022), and broadened into private set union with Linear Private Set Union from Multi-Query Reverse Private Membership Test (2023).

By 2023 the field had clearly split into two engineering-heavy fronts. On the FHE side, the focus shifted from feasibility to making homomorphic computation fast and usable, with ELASM: Error-Latency-Aware Scale Management for Fully Homomorphic Encryption (2023) and later DaCapo: Automatic Bootstrapping Management for Efficient Fully Homomorphic Encryption (2024) automating the painful tuning of scale and bootstrapping. On the oblivious-systems side, EnigMap (2023) and GigaDORAM: Breaking the Billion Address Barrier (2023) scaled oblivious memory to enclave and billion-address regimes. ZK proofs also moved from primitives to applications, with Cheesecloth: Zero-Knowledge Proofs of Real World Vulnerabilities (2023) proving software bugs without disclosing them.

The most recent work (2024-2025) is dominated by privacy-preserving machine learning at scale and by a new wariness about the guarantees these systems actually provide. Scalable Multi-Party Computation Protocols for Machine Learning in the Honest-Majority Setting (2024) and MD-ML (2024) chase faster MPC for training and inference, while Scalable Zero-knowledge Proofs for Non-linear Functions in Machine Learning (2024) brings ZK to ML integrity. Crucially, the community is now attacking its own abstractions: Key Recovery Attacks on Approximate Homomorphic Encryption (2024) breaks CKKS under weak noise-flooding countermeasures, and Holding Secrets Accountable: Auditing Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning (2024) asks whether PPML actually delivers on its promises. The frontier extends to anonymous accountability with zk-promises (2025) and to secure computation on untrusted hardware with Enabling Low-Cost Secure Computing on Untrusted In-Memory Architectures (2025).

milestones.title: XONN: XNOR-based Oblivious Deep Neural Network Inference
milestones.note: made oblivious neural-network inference practical by reducing it to XNOR operations, kicking off the privacy-preserving ML thread

milestones.title: Poseidon: A New Hash Function for Zero-Knowledge Proof Systems
milestones.note: gave ZK proof systems a hash function designed for circuits and became a foundational, heavily cited primitive

milestones.title: Estimating Incidental Collection in Foreign Intelligence Surveillance: Large-Scale Multiparty Private Set Intersection with Union and Sum
milestones.note: scaled multiparty private set intersection to a real, high-stakes surveillance-measurement deployment

milestones.title: ELASM: Error-Latency-Aware Scale Management for Fully Homomorphic Encryption
milestones.note: shifted FHE work toward automated performance tuning, foreshadowing the wave of usability-focused HE systems

milestones.title: Cheesecloth: Zero-Knowledge Proofs of Real World Vulnerabilities
milestones.note: moved ZK from primitives to a concrete security application: proving vulnerabilities without disclosing them

milestones.title: Key Recovery Attacks on Approximate Homomorphic Encryption with Non-Worst-Case Noise Flooding Countermeasures
milestones.note: broke CKKS under weak countermeasures, marking the field's turn toward attacking its own homomorphic abstractions

milestones.title: Scalable Multi-Party Computation Protocols for Machine Learning in the Honest-Majority Setting
milestones.note: represents the current push to make MPC scale for real privacy-preserving machine learning

milestones.title: zk-promises: Anonymous Moderation, Reputation, and Blocking from Anonymous Credentials with Callbacks
milestones.note: extends ZK to anonymous yet accountable systems, signaling the frontier of deployable proof-based applications
